authors: Cohen, W.B., Yang, Z. & Kennedy, R.
title: Detecting trends in forest disturbance and recovery using yearly Landsat time series: 2. TimeSync - Tools for calibration and validation
relevance: TimeSync is the mature, operational form of exactly the paired protocol Searches 41-42 arrived at independently: an interpreter works a SAMPLE POINT's whole TRAJECTORY across all dates at once, assigning change segments rather than classifying each date in isolation. It is the human-interpretation companion to LandTrendr and underpins USFS/LCMAP validation, so our Phase 3 redesign does not need inventing - it needs adopting, with the anchoring safeguards of Search 42 added. Most directly useful paper found for the P3 response design, and it comes with a documented interpretation workflow rather than a principle.

authors: Kennedy, R.E., Yang, Z. & Cohen, W.B.
title: Detecting trends in forest disturbance and recovery using yearly Landsat time series: 1. LandTrendr - Temporal segmentation algorithms
relevance: Segments each pixel's temporal trajectory into straight-line pieces with explicit VERTEX YEARS, capturing abrupt disturbance and gradual recovery in one representation - structurally what a per-crown validity interval wants, a trajectory with breakpoints rather than a smoothed series. The concept transfers; the algorithm may not. LandTrendr assumes YEARLY, seasonally composited observations, and we have 18 IRREGULAR acquisitions with multi-year gaps, one per year at best, and no way to composite away phenology (its acknowledged blind spot, and our Search 30 problem). Adopt the trajectory-with-vertices framing, but do not assume the fitting machinery survives our sampling.
